newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Bangui calm, Central African Republic truce holds.
newsitem.headline: Bangui calm, Central African Republic truce holds.

text.p: Bangui, capital of the Central African Republic, was calm on Sunday after a truce called on Saturday between disaffected soldiers and African peacekeepers held through the night.
Residents said there had been no flare-up in fighting since the four-day truce came into effect at 8 p.m. (1900 GMT) on Saturday.

Mali's widely respected former military leader Amadou Toumani Toure, who brokered a January peace deal to end three army mutinies in under a year, rallied the two sides around the truce as a basis for reviving the peace process.

The Red Cross says the latest clashes, which began on June 20 after an incident involving peacekeepers and mutineers who had yet to rejoin their units, have killed about 100 people, mostly civilians caught in crossfire, and wounded at least 150.

The U.N. refugee agency says more than 60,000 civilians have left the capital for the relative safety of the surrounding countryside. But residents said people were beginning to trickle back to see what was left of their homes and pick through their belongings.
